subject: Cybersecurity
title: The Future of Cyber Norms: Building Rules for Digital Conflict
description: A fast breakdown of The Future of Cyber Norms: Building Rules for Digital Conflict for builders.

hook.text: Nuclear weapons have treaties. Chemical weapons have bans. Cyber weapons have... nothing binding.

buildup.text: The UN Group of Governmental Experts has proposed voluntary norms: don’t attack hospitals, don’t hack elections or infrastructure.

discovery.text: Unlike physical weapons, cyberweapons are invisible, deniable, and easily attributed to others. This makes enforcement impossible.

twist.text: Russia signed the UN cyber norms agreeing not to attack critical infrastructure. Then allegedly attacked Ukraine’s power grid.

climax.text: Cyber norms exist on paper. Enforcement remains the unsolved problem of international cybersecurity governance.

punchline.text: They signed the agreement. Then attacked the power grid.

quiz.question: Why are cyber weapons treaties difficult to enforce?
options: Cyberweapons are invisible, deniable, and difficult to attribute, making verification nearly impossible
Only a few countries have cyber capabilities
